paper_title: Measuring quantum relative entropy with finite-size effect

statement: Remark 9. Recently, the paper [48] studied the estimation of relative entropy with two unknown densities ρ and σ when an estimator of the state is given and the estimator converges to the true density. The analysis [48] is different from ours in the following points. (i) We assume that σ is known, but the paper [48] assumes that it is unknown. (ii) We discuss the optimality of our estimator in various settings. Under the case with fixed d, we optimize the MSE. When d increases, we discuss the sample complexity. But, when an estimator of the state is given, the paper [48] discusses the behavior of the estimator of relative entropy by using the behavior of the estimator. In addition, the paper [48] mentioned that the limiting distribution of the normalized estimator is the normal distribution. When d is fixed, the discussion explains how this problem is reduced to a special case of the parameter estimation with nuisance parameters. The paper [21] also showed that the limiting distribution of the normalized estimator is the normal distribution in the parameter estimation with nuisance parameters.

This implementation of weak Schur sampling was mentioned earlier in [47, Section 1.1.2]. Remark 9. Recently, the paper [48] studied the estimation of relative entropy with two unknown densities ρ and σ when an estimator of the state is given and the estimator converges to the true density. The analysis [48] is different from ours in the following points. (i) We assume that σ is known, but the paper [48] assumes that it is unknown. (ii) We discuss the optimality of our estimator in various settings. Under the case with fixed d, we optimize the MSE. When d increases, we discuss the sample complexity. But, when an estimator of the state is given, the paper [48] discusses the behavior of the estimator of relative entropy by using the behavior of the estimator. In addition, the paper [48] mentioned that the limiting distribution of the normalized estimator is the normal distribution. When d is fixed, the discussion explains how this problem is reduced to a special case of the parameter estimation with nuisance parameters. The paper [21] also showed that the limiting distribution of the normalized estimator is the normal distribution in the parameter estimation with nuisance parameters. 6 Discussion We have studied the estimation of quantum relative entropy D(ρ∥σ) when the second argument σ is known. Our estimator has a good performance in the following two senses. First, when the dimension d is fixed, our estimator attains Cramér-Rao type bound asymptotically. Second, when the dimension d increases, our estimator has sample complexity O(d2 ) under natural assumptions, which greatly improves the sample complexity by the simple application of full tomography [33]. Third, when d is large, although the calculation of our estimator is difficult, we have an alternative estimator whose time complexity is O(d6 polylog(d)). The difference between this alternative estimator and our original estimator approaches zero asymptotically. In the above way, our estimator works well unifiedly, which is a unique feature and did not appear in existing studies [6, 7, 22].
